Phase 48: plugin distribution — impl submission (round 1). Commit fdedab7 on phase-48-plugin-distribution. Implements the plan approved at dc80017, scope B.

What changed:
- plugin/ tree: .claude-plugin/plugin.json (version 3.9.0, tagteam.minVersion 3.9.0), skills/handoff/SKILL.md (byte-identical to the packaged copy — tested), hooks/hooks.json (one SessionStart command: `command -v tagteam … && tagteam hook session-start --plugin-root "$CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT" || true`). Repo-root .claude-plugin/marketplace.json (name tagteam, source ./plugin) → plugin key tagteam@tagteam.
- tagteam/plugin.py (new): plugin_status() — fail-closed detection from $CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/~/.claude: installed_plugins.json schema v2, tagteam@tagteam record with scope user or project+matching realpath, enabledPlugins explicit true in user/project/local settings and false in none, installPath must contain the skill; every other state → not installed with a reason. vendored_skill_provenance() — removable only if the dir holds exactly a regular SKILL.md whose sha256 is in the shipped known set. known_contract_hashes() reads tagteam/data/vendored_contract_hashes.json.
- scripts/contract_hashes.py (new) generates that file from git history (13 distinct contract versions as of 3.9.0 — the plan said 26; that was a miscount on my side, corrected in the doc). Real-world check: bugalizer, harmonic, ns-wip-tests and archive/handoff-test all hash to the 0.6.0 contract; aegis to 3.8.2 — the remove path recognizes every live copy.
- tagteam/setup.py: needs_setup(project_dir, plugin=None) — local skill OR plugin_status().installed; templates+checklists still required. _sync_handoff_skill(): plugin installed → remove (hash-gated) / "nothing to vendor" / "kept …: <reason>", never vendors over a kept dir; plugin absent → vendors as before. main(target, no_plugin=) and run_setup(…, no_plugin=); `tagteam setup [dir] --no-plugin`; no force-remove flag. Prints `plugin: installed (user scope, enabled by …)` / `plugin: not installed (…)` before acting.
- tagteam/headless.py: resolve_skill_path(root, explicit) → (path, "explicit"|"project"|"packaged"); PACKAGED_SKILL_PATH = tagteam/data/.claude/skills/handoff/SKILL.md; HeadlessEngine stores skill_source; validate() errors only when the resolved path is missing (names the source); prompt header is now `=== HANDOFF CONTRACT (<source>) ===`. Plugin cache is never read.
- tagteam/hook.py (new) + `tagteam hook session-start [--plugin-root DIR]` in cli.py: banner line iff tagteam.yaml + well-typed handoff-state.json; skew warning iff plugin.json tagteam.minVersion > tagteam.__version__; every other case silent, exit 0, including unknown args and a plugin root that is a file.
- scripts/release.py: bumps plugin.json version + tagteam.minVersion in the same transaction, regenerates the hash file, refuses when plugin/ and packaged SKILL.md differ or plugin.json is missing; rollback set extended. publish.yml: tag must match plugin.json version; cmp of the two contract copies; contract_hashes.py --check.
- pyproject: package-data "data/*.json". README: plugin install section. Callers of needs_setup (run_setup, session start --launch, worktree._seed_project) unchanged in code; covered by tests.
- Fixture note added at the head of ~/projects/archive/handoff-test/.claude/skills/handoff/SKILL.md (outside this repo; grep of that dir found no consumer of SKILL.md).

Tests (tests/): test_plugin.py (tree/manifests/hooks.json pinned/hash file current/byte-equality; plugin_status matrix 13 cases; provenance 7 cases), test_hook.py (subprocess: silent cases, banner, skew, bad plugin root), test_setup.py (remove path matrix incl. --no-plugin via CLI, upgrade sweep), test_quickstart.py (needs_setup plugin matrix + --launch does not rerun setup), test_worktree.py (user-scope plugin → no rollback and no vendored skill; project-scope → vendored into the worktree), test_headless.py (resolution order, validate without local skill, header), test_release_script.py (fixture grows the plugin tree; lockstep bump, mismatch refusal, dry-run). Plugin state is injected via CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR fixtures (tests/_plugin_env.py), not monkeypatched internals.

Verification: gate: see entry @ fdedab7 (on_submit run). Focused: the 7 touched suites, 289 passed.

NOT done — needs the arbiter: plan criterion 4 / migration step 2 (a full cycle on aegis with the skill served from the plugin, both resolution paths) requires the plugin to be installed through Claude Code (`/plugin marketplace add`), which I cannot do from this session; this is the post-merge canary before the registry sweep (step 4). Also not done: the plan's "registry entry records contract: plugin" line — the registry is a plain list of paths, and changing its schema is out of scope; dropped. Environmental note: the .venv's editable metadata still reports 3.8.2, so a live `tagteam hook session-start --plugin-root plugin` here prints the skew warning (correctly) until the venv is reinstalled.

Round 2 — gate bounce on r1 was tests/test_docs_story.py::test_every_cli_command_is_documented (the new `tagteam hook` subcommand had no README reference line). Added reference lines for `tagteam hook session-start`, `tagteam setup` (plugin handover) and `tagteam setup --no-plugin` in the README command block. Commit: docs-only on top of fdedab7. Everything in the round-1 submission stands unchanged — read that entry for the full change list, tests, and the "NOT done" items (aegis canary needs the plugin installed via Claude Code by the arbiter; registry schema line dropped).

Verification: gate: see entry @ HEAD (on_submit run); focused tests/test_docs_story.py passes.

checked: HEAD 7b117bb

Gate is valid at 7b117bb (1504 passed, 5 skipped), and both manifests pass `claude plugin validate` with only the expected warning for the custom `tagteam` metadata key. Two blocking integration defects remain, and the required canary is still outstanding.

1. The plugin does not preserve the `/handoff` command. Claude Code namespaces plugin skills: a plugin named `tagteam` containing `skills/handoff/SKILL.md` is invoked as `/tagteam:handoff`, whereas the project-local skill is `/handoff`. The official plugin docs explicitly contrast standalone `/hello` with plugin `/plugin-name:hello`. Removing `.claude/skills/handoff/` therefore removes the exact interactive command written throughout the contract, state command, README, and NEXT boxes. Resolve this explicitly: either migrate the complete workflow to `/tagteam:handoff` (including generated state commands, docs, prompts, tests, and compatibility behavior), or retain a safe project-local `/handoff` shim that delegates to the namespaced plugin command. The latter weakens “no vendored contract” but preserves compatibility; whichever route is chosen must have an actual Claude Code discovery/invocation test, not only file-layout tests.

2. `plugin_status()` does not model Claude Code’s effective plugin state safely. Current official docs support install scopes `user`, `project`, and `local`, and managed settings have highest precedence. The implementation accepts only user/project records and reads only user/project/local files; it ignores local-scope installs and, more seriously, can report installed+enabled and delete the vendored skill when managed policy has disabled the plugin. Its “false anywhere wins” rule also differs from documented settings precedence. Use Claude Code’s supported effective-state surface when available: `claude plugin list --json` returns `id`, `scope`, `enabled`, `installPath`, and `projectPath` (verified locally in this review). Run it with the target project as cwd, validate the applicable `tagteam@tagteam` record and skill path, and fail closed on missing CLI, timeout, nonzero exit, malformed JSON, unsupported scope, or ambiguity. If raw-file parsing remains as a fallback, it must never produce a removal-authorizing positive when managed/server state is unknowable. Add local-scope, managed-disabled/effective-disabled, command-failure, malformed-output, and applicable-project tests.

3. Do not approve or sweep migrations until the plan’s aegis canary is actually complete. The lead submission marks criterion 4 NOT done; that canary is especially necessary because it would expose the namespace issue above. After the fix, record an installed-plugin interactive invocation using the chosen public command and a headless turn using the packaged contract. This requires arbiter coordination, but it remains an approved success criterion rather than a post-merge optional check.

Round 3 — all three round-2 items addressed. HEAD dbfddfe (commits a9ea5b1, 9bc8bcb, 29e887f, dbfddfe on top of 7b117bb).

1. Namespace — arbiter ruled: migrate to `/tagteam:handoff` (AskUserQuestion, recorded under "Decided by the arbiter"). Contract text: every command usage → `/tagteam:handoff`, NEXT box widened, plus a "one contract, three ways in" paragraph (`/tagteam:handoff` via plugin; `/handoff` where a project still vendors the skill; `tagteam contract` for agents without plugin skills). New tagteam/contract.py: handoff_command(root) → `/handoff` iff a local .claude/skills/handoff/SKILL.md exists, else `/tagteam:handoff`; used by watcher (advance + done nudge), launch intents, worktree kickoff, gate "tell X to run …"; parse_start_command accepts both names. Finding the plan missed: the reviewer is Codex, which has no Claude plugins and read the contract from the path in the state command — a migrated project would have left it with nothing. STANDARD_TURN_COMMAND (contract.py, used by cycle.py + headless) is now "Read the handoff contract (`tagteam contract`; in Claude Code: /tagteam:handoff) and handoff-state.json, then act on your turn"; `tagteam contract [--path]` (new) prints the packaged contract. README/how-tagteam-works migrated; priming box text updated. Discovery/invocation test: see 3.

2. Detection — plugin_status() now runs `claude plugin list --json` with the project as cwd and uses its effective `enabled`; applicable scopes user / project / local (projectPath realpath == project); fails closed on missing CLI, timeout, non-zero exit, malformed/non-array JSON, unsupported scope, ambiguous (conflicting applicable records), missing installPath/skill, and a nonexistent project dir. Raw-file parsing removed entirely (no fallback can authorize removal). TAGTEAM_CLAUDE_BIN overrides the executable ("" = none); tests/conftest.py sets it so the suite never touches the real CLI; tests/_plugin_env.py provides a fake `claude`. Tests: tests/test_plugin.py::TestPluginStatus — 20 cases incl. local scope, effective-disabled, enabled-missing, ambiguous, exit≠0, malformed, timeout, not-executable, cwd verification, and the exact record shape from `claude plugin list --json` 2.1.251.

3. Canary — both paths done and recorded in docs/phases/plugin-distribution.md "Canary record". Headless: throwaway migrated project, real `tagteam watch --mode headless` reviewer turn; log `headless: contract from packaged (…/tagteam/data/.claude/skills/handoff/SKILL.md)` (new log line), `turn ok — reviewer APPROVE at round 1 (13645 ms)`, one cycle-writing call. Interactive: plugin installed via `claude plugin marketplace add <this checkout>` + `claude plugin install tagteam@tagteam --scope user` (the arbiter approved; done through the CLI); on aegis `tagteam setup` printed `removed vendored handoff skill (3.8.2 contract) — served by the plugin`, needs_setup → False, handoff_command → /tagteam:handoff, hook prints the banner, and `claude -p "/tagteam:handoff status"` in aegis (no vendored skill present) executed the plugin skill and produced the status banner + NEXT box. Verbatim output in the phase doc.

Finding from the canary, fixed: the arbiter's PATH tagteam is the 3.9.0 uv tool (no `hook` subcommand) and prints "Unknown command: hook" to stdout, exit 1 — the first hooks.json relayed that into the session. hooks.json now: `command -v tagteam … && out="$(tagteam hook session-start --plugin-root "$CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT" 2>/dev/null)" && [ -n "$out" ] && printf '%s\n' "$out" || true`. tests/test_hook.py::TestHookCommandShell runs the literal command under /bin/sh with no tagteam / an old tagteam / the real one. Consequence noted in the doc: below 3.10 the skew warning cannot fire (the subcommand doesn't exist) — the hook is silent instead.

Also: vendored_contract_hashes.json regenerated (14 versions now — the new contract is one of them; the plan's "26" was my miscount, corrected). aegis is migrated ahead of its CLI until 3.10 ships + `uv tool upgrade tagteam` (its 3.9.0 needs_setup would re-vendor on `session start --launch`; harmless, noted). Two test assertion sets flipped to the namespaced command for fixture projects that have no local skill (test_roadmap ×3, test_cockpit_api ×1). One order-dependent flake observed once in a subset run (tests/test_terminal_backend.py::test_iterm_reexports_session_file_helpers) — passes alone with and without these changes, and in the r2 gate run.

Verification: gate: see entry @ dbfddfe (on_submit run). Focused: 17 touched suites, 793 passed before the last two commits; hook/plugin suites 63 passed at HEAD.

The gate is valid at 5bb22a3 (1524 passed, 5 skipped). The namespace design, effective `claude plugin list --json` detection, hook compatibility, and direct interactive discovery test are sound. Two required fixes remain.

1. Complete the runtime namespace/source migration. Four user-facing paths still emit instructions that fail after the local skill is removed:
- `tagteam/session.py::PRIME_MESSAGE` tells every newly launched agent to read `.claude/skills/handoff/SKILL.md`.
- `tagteam/lead_chat.py::FIRST_TURN_HEADER` says the contract is at that same missing path.
- `tagteam/panel.py` manual-panel fallback says `run /handoff`.
- `tagteam/gatekeeper.py` manual `gate run` pass path says `run /handoff` (the on-submit path was fixed, but this second path was not).

Use `STANDARD_TURN_COMMAND` or a centralized project-aware renderer instead of duplicating literals. The panel/gate messages should use `handoff_command(root)`. Add focused tests for migrated and vendored projects, and add an audit regression over runtime user-facing strings so a bare local-path instruction or unconditional `/handoff` does not survive elsewhere. The README's descriptive legacy mentions are not the issue; executable prompts and next-step output are.

2. Finish the approved canary rather than relabeling a partial smoke test. The phase success criterion requires a full plan+impl cycle on aegis and verification that the reviewer turn carries both `PROJECT CONTEXT` and `CHANGE SURFACE`. The recorded evidence is (a) one plan-review approval in a throwaway project and (b) `/tagteam:handoff status` against an already-completed aegis cycle. That proves plugin discovery and packaged headless loading separately, but it is not a full plan+impl cycle on aegis and does not record the required context/surface blocks. Run and record the named disposable aegis plan+impl cycle, including the impl reviewer turn's contract source and both injected blocks. The arbiter already authorized installation/canary work, so this is completion of the existing criterion, not a new migration sweep.

One small test correction while touching this area: parenthesize `tests/test_plugin.py::TestContractCommand::test_path`; its current `and ... or ...` assertion can pass on a nonzero command whenever stdout ends with `SKILL.md`.

Round 5 — both round-4 items and the test correction. HEAD = this commit (5646e7c + canary record).

1. Runtime strings. New contract.CONTRACT_HOWTO ("the handoff contract (`tagteam contract`; in Claude Code: /tagteam:handoff)"); STANDARD_TURN_COMMAND is built from it (string unchanged, corpus intact). session.PRIME_MESSAGE now reads "Read tagteam.yaml to see your role, then read <CONTRACT_HOWTO> for the workflow." lead_chat.FIRST_TURN_HEADER takes handoff_cmd=handoff_command(root) at both format sites (first-turn and codex-replay) — "invoked as /tagteam:handoff (or read with `tagteam contract`)" on a migrated project, `/handoff` on a vendored one. panel.py manual fallback and gatekeeper.py manual `gate run` pass path print `tell the reviewer to run {handoff_command(root)}`. Tests (tests/test_plugin.py::TestRuntimeStringsAudit): audit over tagteam/*.py — no ".claude/skills/handoff/SKILL.md" outside the four path-owning modules (contract/headless/plugin/setup), no `run|type|paste|tell … to run /handoff` not built from handoff_command; prime message names both routes; lead-chat header migrated vs vendored; gate/panel next-lines project-aware (both flavors).

2. Canary — full plan+impl cycle on the aegis tree, recorded verbatim under "Canary record". Disposable git worktree of ~/projects/QA (branch canary/phase-48-plugin from ac13d14; the arbiter's working tree untouched), tagteam.yaml with real headless providers (lead claude, reviewer codex; panel off), setup removed the vendored 3.8.2 contract, doc-only phase phase-48-canary. `tagteam watch --mode headless` drove everything: plan r1 codex REQUEST_CHANGES → claude revised → r2 codex APPROVE; impl started with `--command "/tagteam:handoff start phase-48-canary impl"` (single-phase mode does not auto-advance) → claude implemented + committed + cycle init impl → codex impl turn logged `contract from packaged`, `project context from CLAUDE.md`, `change surface 2 path(s)` → APPROVE. Disclosure: aegis main has no root CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md, so the branch carries a small labeled CLAUDE.md — without it the block is absent by design (Phase 47), not by defect. Observation: codex's sandboxed turns used the arbiter's PATH tagteam (uv tool 3.9.0) for their cycle writes, so those wrote the old standard command string — the mixed-version window that closes at release.

3. test_path parenthesized: asserts returncode == 0 and the resolved path equals the packaged contract.

Verification: gate: see entry @ HEAD (on_submit run). Focused: 332 passed across plugin/session_prime/iterm/terminal/lead_chat/panel/gatekeeper/docs_story at 5646e7c.
